evidenceBoundary.engineeringEvidence: Repository facts, deterministic audits, unit tests, browser tests, CI and exact-commit deployment checks.
evidenceBoundary.productEvidence: Machine first-use inspection and rubric-based product inference; useful for design decisions but not a child outcome claim.

benchmarkCases.name: DragonBox Algebra
benchmarkCases.mechanism: Manipulating cards to isolate a box gradually becomes manipulation of numbers and variables; the mathematical transformation is the puzzle action.
benchmarkCases.adopt: Require every Equation Slider move to express visible mathematical meaning.
benchmarkCases.exclude: Hidden identity progress and a commercial subscription wrapper.
benchmarkCases.uncertainty: Vendor description; no independent current playtest or transfer evidence.

benchmarkCases.name: DragonBox Numbers
benchmarkCases.mechanism: Visible quantities can be stacked, sliced, combined, sorted and compared across open and challenge modes.
benchmarkCases.adopt: Reuse stable visible quantity models across Math World interactions.
benchmarkCases.exclude: Decorative operations, daily cadence and subscription mechanics.
benchmarkCases.uncertainty: Advertised learning effects were not independently established.

benchmarkCases.name: DragonBox Big Numbers
benchmarkCases.mechanism: Gathering and trading resources requires arithmetic while visible quantities and operations grow in complexity.
benchmarkCases.adopt: Let mathematical operations cause visible world consequences and representations.
benchmarkCases.exclude: Operation grind and collectible furnishing as the primary reason to calculate.
benchmarkCases.uncertainty: Product listing, not outcome evidence; pacing was not independently tested.

benchmarkCases.name: Osmo Numbers
benchmarkCases.mechanism: Physical dots and digits are arranged, added, removed or connected while the screen responds in real time and accepts multiple solutions.
benchmarkCases.adopt: Recognize several valid strategies and give immediate causal feedback in Math modules.
benchmarkCases.exclude: Proprietary hardware and sensor assumptions in an offline browser portfolio.
benchmarkCases.uncertainty: Hardware accessibility, recognition reliability and transfer are not established by the sales page.

benchmarkCases.name: Pokemon Smile
benchmarkCases.mechanism: Camera-detected brushing drives the game action, with bounded session timing and stated no-upload handling of live video.
benchmarkCases.adopt: Use it only as a strong conceptual example that the real or learning action can be the game input.
benchmarkCases.exclude: Camera tracking, reminders, daily collection, awards and sensor-dependent success.
benchmarkCases.uncertainty: Recognition can fail; the official site does not guarantee habit or preference outcomes.

benchmarkCases.name: Toca Boca World
benchmarkCases.mechanism: A persistent open world supports child-authored stories, characters and homes across a large connected catalogue.
benchmarkCases.adopt: Describe My Game World honestly as a hub until it has a meaningful child-authored core loop.
benchmarkCases.exclude: Content-volume race, storefront framing, weekly gifts, scarcity and limited-time packs.
benchmarkCases.uncertainty: Scale and brand strength confound comparison; no transfer evidence.

benchmarkCases.name: Sago Mini World
benchmarkCases.mechanism: Many small creative and tinkering activities sit in one calm, offline-capable app without points or time limits.
benchmarkCases.adopt: Merge small experiences into discoverable world modules while retaining calm self-chosen replay.
benchmarkCases.exclude: Subscription/content treadmill and activity count as a proxy for depth.

benchmarkCases.name: Pok Pok
benchmarkCases.mechanism: An open-ended digital playroom emphasizes calm toys, low-language affordances and no winning, losing or child-facing purchases.
benchmarkCases.adopt: Use low-language affordances, experimentation, co-play and pressure-free stations.
benchmarkCases.exclude: Turning the whole portfolio into an unstructured toybox or importing cloud storage patterns.
benchmarkCases.uncertainty: Intuitiveness and non-addictive language are first-party claims.

benchmarkCases.name: Khan Academy Kids
benchmarkCases.mechanism: A recommended adaptive path coexists with an independently browsable library of activities and creative material.
benchmarkCases.adopt: Keep a recommended next action separate from free exploration, without overstating mastery.
benchmarkCases.exclude: Opaque cloud personalization, accounts and parent metrics dominating the child surface.
benchmarkCases.uncertainty: Adaptation quality and transfer were not audited.

benchmarkCases.name: PBS KIDS Games
benchmarkCases.mechanism: A broad free, ad-free and offline-capable catalogue uses familiar world and character entry points.
benchmarkCases.adopt: Use curated world continuity and a few intelligible entry lenses instead of exposing the compatibility registry as a card wall.
benchmarkCases.exclude: Catalogue size as proof of quality or licensed-character appeal as the core mechanic.
benchmarkCases.uncertainty: Individual game integration and accessibility vary.

benchmarkCases.name: Sesame Street App
benchmarkCases.mechanism: A child-safe games catalogue can be filtered by character or learning area.
benchmarkCases.adopt: Support child-facing world navigation and parent-facing learning lenses from one truth source.
benchmarkCases.exclude: Video catalogue logic in the play loop or account requirements for local play.
benchmarkCases.uncertainty: Aggregate platform claim; individual games differ.

benchmarkCases.name: Prodigy Math
benchmarkCases.mechanism: A coherent fantasy world and adaptive curriculum surround questions that power battles, pets, quests and reward layers.
benchmarkCases.adopt: Keep only coherent world framing and carefully bounded adaptation.
benchmarkCases.exclude: Detached question/battle loop, daily and seasonal quests, PvP, rare collections, paid reward asymmetry and FOMO.
benchmarkCases.uncertainty: The separation judgment is a design inference from official mechanics, not an outcome study.

benchmarkCases.name: ABCmouse Classic
benchmarkCases.mechanism: A sequenced learning path and broad curriculum are surrounded by tickets, rooms, avatars, pets and lesson prizes.
benchmarkCases.adopt: A recommended path may coexist with free choice and voiced instructions.
benchmarkCases.exclude: Ticket currency, shopping/pet unlock loops, surprise rewards, activity-volume targets and premium gates.
benchmarkCases.uncertainty: Breadth and sequencing may help, but this source does not establish causal outcomes.

researchSources.citation: Habgood & Ainsworth (2011), Motivating Children to Learn Effectively: Exploring the Value of Intrinsic Integration in Educational Games
researchSources.supportedClaim: In two studies, an intrinsically integrated game produced better fixed-time learning and substantially more free-choice play than an extrinsic version.
researchSources.implication: The curriculum operation should be the core game mechanic; this directly motivates the Equation visible-change repair.
researchSources.boundary: Small, specific studies with ages 7-11; not a portfolio-wide causal guarantee.

researchSources.citation: Plass, Homer & Kinzer (2015), Foundations of Game-Based Learning
researchSources.supportedClaim: Game-based learning depends on interacting cognitive, motivational, affective and sociocultural processes and is distinct from adding gamification.
researchSources.implication: Audit mechanics, feedback, affect and choice separately; playful styling is not learning evidence.
researchSources.boundary: An integrative framework, not a single causal intervention.

researchSources.citation: Wouters et al. (2013), A Meta-Analysis of the Cognitive and Motivational Effects of Serious Games
researchSources.supportedClaim: Across 77 comparisons, serious games had small learning and retention advantages but no significant motivation advantage; supplementation and repeated sessions mattered.
researchSources.implication: Expect modest conditional effects and use replay/contextual support rather than assuming game format motivates or teaches by itself.
researchSources.boundary: Heterogeneous older studies; not specific to this family portfolio.

researchSources.supportedClaim: Modality, personalization, pretraining, coaching and self-explanation can add value while irrelevant decoration consumes limited processing.
researchSources.implication: Prefer micro-demonstration, contextual coaching and concise reflection; reduce decoration during difficult actions.
researchSources.boundary: Findings vary by task and setting.

researchSources.citation: Ryan, Rigby & Przybylski (2006), The Motivational Pull of Video Games
researchSources.supportedClaim: Perceived autonomy and competence related to enjoyment and preference; relatedness also mattered in multiplayer contexts.
researchSources.implication: Offer bounded meaningful choice, interpretable competence feedback and optional family co-play without prize pressure.
researchSources.boundary: Mostly general-game and non-child evidence; not a learning-effect proof.

researchSources.supportedClaim: Effective formative feedback is supportive, specific, credible and timely, with manageable elaboration focused on learning.
researchSources.implication: Explain what changed, why it did not work and one calm next action without revealing the full solution.
researchSources.boundary: Broad educational review; timing still needs mechanic-specific validation.

researchSources.citation: Wood, Bruner & Ross (1976), The Role of Tutoring in Problem Solving
researchSources.supportedClaim: Scaffolding can control difficult elements while preserving the child's meaningful work.
researchSources.implication: Use a fading hint ladder and return control for the final meaningful action.
researchSources.boundary: Small classic tutor-child task; design model rather than automatic digital effect.

researchSources.citation: Skene et al. (2022), Can Guidance During Play Enhance Children's Learning and Development in Educational Contexts?
researchSources.supportedClaim: Guided play exceeded direct instruction for some early-math, shape and task-switching outcomes, but not many others; implementation was heterogeneous.
researchSources.implication: Combine clear goals with child choice and flexible prompts, especially in Math World.
researchSources.boundary: Results differed by outcome and comparator; no universal child-outcome claim.

designPrinciples.principle: Learning action must be game action.
designPrinciples.portfolioMeaning: Inspect Equation, Make Target, Clock, Array, Pinyin and Memory for detached answer/reward wrappers.

designPrinciples.principle: Every legal action needs a perceptible causal consequence.
designPrinciples.portfolioMeaning: State identity, representation, feedback and world response must agree.
Offer a recommended next action plus real alternatives, replay and retreat without loss.
Use immediate semantic feedback and one calm recovery action, not rarity or currency pressure.
Micro-demo, critical-feature cue, partial hint and optional worked support must preserve the final meaningful action.

designPrinciples.principle: A world product needs child-authored consequences.
designPrinciples.portfolioMeaning: My Game World remains a hub until it has a learning/play loop; do not invent V2 progression in this cycle.
No daily quests, streaks, FOMO, battle passes, loot rarity or paid advantage.

designPrinciples.principle: Separate products, modules, compatibility and engines.
designPrinciples.portfolioMeaning: A retained GameDefinition or save key does not imply a child-facing card.
Do not import cameras, accounts, cloud profiles, telemetry or proprietary hardware assumptions.
Machine review cannot establish child enjoyment, comprehension, retention or learning effect.

independentReviews.identityContract: Reviewed against the current release candidate; any later tracked mutation invalidates this review; the release tag and exact-SHA readback bind the immutable final tree.
independentReviews.reviewerIndependence: Read-only subagent; no product edits; separate browser origin and gameplay-first rubric.
independentReviews.keyFinding: Keep four active products; converge Make Target and Memory duplicate cards; reject Equation Slider actions whose mathematical display does not change while retaining every level and compatibility contract.

findings.resolution: Same-visible adjacent moves are rejected without mutating moves or state, calm feedback explains why, and solver/hints use the visible-move graph; all 82 affected levels remain solvable.
Classic and My Game World now project the four active products from one truth while duplicate Make Target and Memory cards retire without deleting their playable implementations.
Make Target legacy state migrates to version 1 only on a safe write boundary, reload restores it, and a future-version save remains byte-exact and read-only through interaction.
Affected-gate routing now selects the Equation S release, level, visual/geometry and playtest profiles plus the changed Hanzi wheel profile.

Two redundant whole-catalog audit recomputations that made the 445-test gate timeout were removed; the dedicated live audit still matches the generated deterministic hash, targeted tests pass 16/16, and the complete unit suite passes 445/445.

The decorative Hanzi path light now reproduces its intended in-bounds appearance without adding an invisible 8% document tail; its aria-hidden wrapper uses overflow:hidden instead of the globally unauthorized overflow:clip, and the static scroll contract plus strict desktop, mobile and tablet screenshots pass.

The Classic parent-world return proof now waits for the lazy public wrapper's terminal surface before locating and hit-testing its control; slower CI can no longer mistake the intermediate route-loading state for a missing return path.

independentReviews.identityContract: Reviewed against the current release candidate; any later tracked mutation invalidates this review; the release tag and exact-SHA readback bind the immutable final tree.
independentReviews.reviewerIndependence: Read-only subagent; no product edits; learning/portfolio-first rubric independent from gameplay review.
independentReviews.keyFinding: Separate mount definitions, active products, world modules, compatibility surfaces and shared engines; keep routes and saves independent from card visibility and retain authentic-child outcomes as unknown.

findings.resolution: The durable truth now distinguishes 9 mount definitions, 4 active products, 11 world modules, 6 compatibility surfaces and 2 shared engines.
Portfolio Evolution remains RELEASE_BOUND until exact tag, CI and Pages readback; Natural-use Observation remains ACTIVE and no child or family acceptance is inferred.
Portfolio evidence now has runtime structural validation, substantive review findings and dispositions, and the evolution checker is enforced by CI, Pages and the full readiness workflow.
The six-hats decision record now states 6 compatibility surfaces and the checker binds that count to the canonical layer truth.
Real-child comprehension, preference, learning and retention remain explicit unknowns and are future observation inputs, not blockers or synthetic claims in this release.
CI now installs Chromium and executes, rather than merely resolves, the full affected-gate closure selected from the exact push or pull-request range.

The historical English V2 release builder keeps its six-card proof isolated from later Portfolio projections, while validating product-tag ancestry and only the English evidence inputs it actually consumes.

The compatibility-safe Classic return contract is verified only after its asynchronous public wrapper is visible, preserving the actual two-step product-to-Classic-to-parent-world path without weakening control, route or hit-test assertions.

definitions.topProblem: The compatibility/content/asset surface is large, and machine evidence cannot establish child pacing or return value.

Whether chapter pacing, return value or long-term learning is effective in family use.

definitions.sharedEngineImpact: Continues consuming memory-match through Chinese Memory.

definitions.title: 算式滑轨

definitions.topProblem: 82 levels contained a legal adjacent tile-identity change with no visible mathematical change; 45 exposed it initially.
unknowns: Whether children understand the new rejection explanation without adult help.
Whether rejecting the edge is preferable in lived play to reauthoring the affected reels.

definitions.routeImpact: Both canonical Math World and Classic alternate routes retained.
definitions.saveImpact: Existing save namespace and published level IDs retained.
definitions.sharedEngineImpact: Game-owned reducer, evaluator, solver and generator retained.

notDo: No sixth station in this cycle
No world-wide mastery claim from visits

surfaceCoverage.remainingCoverage: All remaining manifest surfaces are covered by the affected content/simulation, portfolio smoke, hit-test, scroll, accessibility, save and product profile suites; no manifest surface is intentionally excluded.

equationVisibleChangeAudit.algorithm: BFS over (reel indexes, required-tile bitmask, target bitmask), comparing all edges with a graph that removes moves whose selected visible value does not change.
equationVisibleChangeAudit.childVisibleDecision: Reject a same-display adjacent attempt without state or move-count mutation; explain the absent mathematical change and direct the player to the opposite visible move.

agreements: Four active products: Hanzi, Math World, English World and Equation Slider.
Make Target belongs in Math World and should not keep a duplicate Classic card.
Memory is a shared engine/world activity and should not keep a generic Classic card.
Clock and Array remain Math World modules; Pinyin definition is compatibility-only.
Classic remains a four-card alternate launcher, not product truth.
My Game World remains a hub, not a learning product.
reviewReconciliation.resolvedDifference: Gameplay review preferred reauthoring repeated reels; exhaustive engineering evidence showed no required same-display edge and a maximum one-move cost. The implemented minimum compatible repair rejects only the invisible edge, preserves all published levels/IDs/saves, provides explicit causal feedback, and binds solver/hints to visible moves. Level reauthoring is therefore deferred unless later evidence shows the rejection itself is confusing.
